market_context: Nasdaq 100 futures were down about 1% and S&P futures about 0.3-0.5% after Alphabet missed on earnings and free cash flow (GOOGL down about 10% pre-market). ServiceNow and Fortinet also fell sharply, while Microsoft rose about 4% on strong Azure results. The 10Y yield is about 5%, markets price roughly an 85% chance of a December Fed hike, and Q3 GDP came in at 3.4% against 3.1% expected. Amazon and Intel report after the close, and PCE inflation is also due today.

predictions.reasoning: Alphabet missed Q3 revenue and EPS and reported negative free cash flow of about $9B, which revived AI capex worries. It was down more than 10% pre-market, and search growth of 12% against about 15% expected is a thesis-level disappointment. Post-earnings drops of this size usually hold through the close.

Nasdaq 100 futures were down about 1% to 1.4% overnight on the Alphabet miss and software selloff (NOW -18%, FTNT -26%). A 5% 10Y yield and rate-hike pricing add pressure on tech valuations. Microsoft's gain only partly offsets this.

Microsoft beat on EPS ($4.89 vs $4.73) and revenue ($92.28B vs $90.63B), helped by Azure strength. It was up about 3.5-4% pre-market against a weak Nasdaq. Beat-and-raise reactions tend to hold into the close.

The S&P opened about 0.5% lower, dragged by Alphabet and software stocks. Strong GDP at 3.4% raises Fed-hike odds, and the 10Y rose to about 5.05%. Dow strength and Microsoft limit the downside, and Amazon earnings after the close add uncertainty.
